name: camera-lens
title: Camera Lens
description: A scene seen through a lens instead of rendered flat: softness growing toward the corners, bright text blooming, red and blue fringing at the edges, a gentle barrel bend and a falloff in the light. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a render queue list; title, rows and background from variables), not over the host video. Subtle enough to leave running under a whole shot.
useWhen: A screencast looks sterile and should read as filmed: the cheapest way to stop a recording looking like a render.
You want a treatment subtle enough to leave running under a whole demo.
avoidWhen: The story is a tube being watched: use crt-screen.
The story is a worn signal: use vhs-filter.
The story is the recorder the shot was written to: use security-cam.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Aberration
variables.description: Red and blue fringing toward the edges.

variables.label: Vignette
variables.description: Falloff of the light toward the corners.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. The lens look is soft; 0.75 matches 1 in the stills.
